archive_19_001.speaker: narrator
archive_19_001.text: Yue spent her one hundred and twenty-sixth day off looking for a new pair of stockings. The village seller insisted the pair on his stall was brown. Yue thought it was the colour of a wet mouse attempting to appear respectable. The seller said that description would cost extra if she wanted it embroidered. She bought the plain pair and sat on the assembly-room step to examine the seams. Snow still filled the gutters, although the sunny side of the square had begun releasing a steady trickle into its cleared drain.

archive_19_002.speaker: narrator
archive_19_002.text: He Xi passed with a parcel tied so elaborately that Yue asked whether it was likely to escape. He said the customer had packed it himself and instructed the courier not to alter the knots. At the next doorway, the receiving woman opened the parcel to find an ordinary wooden bowl. She examined the knots more closely than the bowl. He Xi waited for her signature and the agreed return cover. Yue could hear her asking whether her brother had paid for a knot or a delivery. He answered that the price included neither an artistic judgment nor an insult.

archive_19_003.speaker: narrator
archive_19_003.text: When he came back, Yue showed him the stockings. He said they looked durable. She asked whether that was a courier's expression for ugly. He said it was the expression for something which might remain useful after a beautiful pair had surrendered to the road. She put them away before the seller heard him. He Xi had to continue his paid loop, and Yue did not ask him to escort her unassigned shopping. She watched him take the ordinary cleared lane, carrying a customer's return envelope and an expression which suggested he was still thinking about the knots.

archive_19_004.speaker: narrator
archive_19_004.text: The return envelope reached the archive after its public desk had opened. It belonged to a farmer who had received a family history copied by his elder brother. A phrase about the brothers' late aunt appeared to grant the farmer the western shed. He wanted the archive to recognise it because the family book had been copied from a registered house paper. Luo read the offered page under the farmer's permission and asked for the registered paper's reference. The farmer supplied an old catalogue number and a story about how the aunt had always favoured him.

archive_19_005.speaker: narrator
archive_19_005.text: The family page contained the words may use during repairs. Its copied heading said permanent western shed grant. Luo showed the farmer the difference without asking whether the aunt had been affectionate. The man pointed to the beautiful heading, written in his brother's careful hand, and said his brother understood property better than anyone in the family. Dai fetched the public catalogue reference and discovered that it described a repair-use agreement, with no transfer mentioned. The archive could supply the admitted wording. The farmer would still need the appropriate registry to determine its present legal use.

archive_19_006.speaker: narrator
archive_19_006.text: The farmer grew angry with the brother rather than the archive. He demanded a statement calling the heading fraudulent. Dai said the archive had no evidence of the brother's intention and no authority to decide that accusation. The copied heading was unsupported by this source. She could state that clearly enough to be useful. The farmer asked whether careless was a word she could write. She said she could describe the exact difference instead. He left with the checked extract and the receiving desk's address, still muttering about a man whose elegant handwriting had become expensive.

archive_19_007.speaker: narrator
archive_19_007.text: Luo watched him cross the yard and remembered how often a heading could do work its paragraph never authorised. He had wanted to laugh at the man's faith in beautiful lettering. Then he saw Dai's corrected catalogue chain on the table. His own old wrapper note lay beneath it. He closed the window against a new cold draught and returned to the current application. The afternoon did not require a confession from either custodian, but it had removed the comfortable distance they might have kept from the farmer's mistake.

archive_19_008.speaker: narrator
archive_19_008.text: Dai asked the assistant to add the shed example to the public lesson file only if the farmer agreed to anonymised use. He had not yet offered that purpose. Luo suggested inventing a different shed for the class instead. Yue, returning from her free day, heard the suggestion and liked it. They could teach a copied heading's limits without recruiting an annoyed family into the programme. She drew a goat beside the invented shed. Dai asked whether the goat had permission to use it. Yue said that would be the first question for the pupils.

archive_19_009.speaker: narrator
archive_19_009.text: That evening, the regional preservation office's reply came through the lower relay. Its clerk had reviewed the two loaned cases against the actual seasonal delay. The office proposed extending the mountain loan through the end of the accepted spring term, with a specific return check before that date. Approved transport of the six selected public originals could use the first case once a current loaded route passed. The second could remain for bounded local emergency use and be returned empty after the private packets no longer needed it. The letter enclosed spaces for the archive's acceptance.

archive_19_010.speaker: narrator
archive_19_010.text: Tan checked the cases before Dai answered. The first still held its six supported public instruments with the seals and condition notes intact. The second had held the authorised emergency move's private packets; those now rested separately on the restored dry supports under their existing custody terms. Tan removed the empty compartments, checked the lining and recorded one scuffed exterior corner. The scuff did not threaten the shell, but it belonged on the return condition sheet. Luo carried the empty case to the accessible shelf and nearly banged it against the doorway while discussing careful handling.

archive_19_011.speaker: tan_ke
archive_19_011.text: Stop speaking for one moment and look at the door. I agree that the case is sound. I do not agree that a sound case makes every person carrying it wide enough to fit through a narrow opening. Turn it after the handles are clear. We can debate the condition record when it is resting on the shelf. If you add a second scuff while insisting the first is harmless, I shall make you draw both.

archive_19_012.speaker: narrator
archive_19_012.text: He obeyed and set the case down without another mark. The assistant laughed, then checked that the return inventory named all removable supports. Dai signed the mutual extension on day one hundred and twenty-seven and sent its acceptance through the agreed relay. The loan continued because both parties had actually accepted its revised dates. The selected public transfer remained pending a safe carriage. Yue entered the new return check in the shared queue and drew no goat beside it. Equipment could acquire a comic history without losing the seriousness of its destination.

archive_19_013.speaker: narrator
archive_19_013.text: The renewed case terms made Luo ask about the public references left on the mountain. One complaint register's local copy had a reader's pencil question in its separate consultation sleeve. The question challenged a date beside an acknowledgement number. The original remained in the packed public case; its visible source had supported the date when checked. Dai proposed inspecting the reference with the original under Tan's ordinary handling plan before transport. If the reference had an error, keeping it local would make the error easier to reach rather than make access good.

archive_19_014.speaker: narrator
archive_19_014.text: The next morning, Tan opened the public case under the authorised comparison procedure and supported the register without forcing its stiff cover flat. Yue read the acknowledgement date while the assistant read the reference independently. They matched. The pencil question concerned the date when the petition had reached a different office, not the archive acknowledgement. Luo wrote an explanation distinguishing the two events and sent it to the reader's chosen receiving desk. The original went back into its assessed support and the resealed case gained a dated opening record.

archive_19_015.speaker: narrator
archive_19_015.text: The reader's question stayed in the consultation history with the response. Luo did not erase it merely because the copied date had passed the check. A later person might bring the same confusion, and the two receiving events were easier to distinguish with a plain note. Dai shortened one sentence which sounded as though the reader had failed a test. Yue proposed drawing two small desks in the school example. The assistant asked whether both desks would contain goats. Yue said only if the pupils insisted on making archives more lively than the staff could manage.

archive_19_016.speaker: narrator
archive_19_016.text: On the one hundred and twenty-eighth afternoon, Tan received the publication board's request for a direct comparison with the old treatment notebook. Her former master had supplied her working notes under a limited professional inquiry permission. The board wanted Tan's account of the pupil pattern and the later revisions, with references rather than a demand that it adopt her preferred title. Tan sat beside the cold window reading the request. She had spent so long anticipating refusal that a serious question felt like another way of losing her balance.

archive_19_017.speaker: narrator
archive_19_017.text: She showed Yue the requested fields. The first asked for the earliest surviving design; the second asked for the final plate used in the school book. Between them lay revisions made by several hands. Tan wanted her own invention recognised without pretending she had also made those later changes. She took a blank sheet and wrote the stages in separate columns. Her first design looked smaller there than in the years of resentment she had carried. It also looked unmistakably hers. She began the reply before she could decide that being accurate had made it insufficient.

archive_19_018.speaker: narrator
archive_19_018.text: Cold returned before dawn on day one hundred and twenty-nine. The yard's previous trickle had become a bright strip beneath the steps, and the keeper marked it before the first resident crossed. The stove went back to the full daily charcoal issue. Yue looked at the frozen line from the safe doorway and remembered the market seller's claim that spring would arrive when his remaining gloves sold. The gloves were still there. Neither the weather nor the seller had gained an authority by wanting the same useful event.

archive_19_019.speaker: narrator
archive_19_019.text: A district maintenance crew arrived on the checked foot route with its own food and tools. Its surveyor wanted to examine the ravine outlet before proposing the thaw repair. The lower shelf remained closed under the winter warning; nobody needed to stand on it to make the danger look convincing. Tan showed the marked observation positions above the channel and the district's previous support notes. The surveyor used the safe positions to read the outlet face, then requested an ordinary long measuring line. The line belonged to his crew and arrived with its inspected reel.

archive_19_020.speaker: narrator
archive_19_020.text: Yue's assigned task was to copy the actual measurements called from the safe stations. She kept the sheet clear of the wet rail and read each number back before the next point. The surveyor saw a loose ice mass hanging above the far notch, where warming runoff had undermined its attachment and the renewed freeze concealed the gap. He moved the observation station farther back and called everyone behind the marked barrier. A porter objected that the far notch could be reached in three steps. The surveyor asked him to count how many steps the ice would need.

archive_19_021.speaker: narrator
archive_19_021.text: They waited until the crew could release the small obstructing piece from the remote safe side with its ordinary tool. The larger overhang stayed beyond that work plan and kept the lower shelf closed. When the smaller piece fell, it struck the empty channel with a sound that came back through the stone as a blunt crack. Yue's pencil stopped between two figures. The porter looked at the place where he had proposed standing. He made no joke afterwards, but helped reset the barrier where the surveyor required it. Their measurements continued from the revised positions.

archive_19_022.speaker: narrator
archive_19_022.text: The surveyor's plan separated the winter obstruction from the damaged retaining stones beneath it. A thaw crew would need a verified approach, fitted supports and an assessed clearing order before restoring the full outlet. The district maintenance account would fund that qualified work under its public drainage duty. It would not be paid from the archive's meals or Yue's wages. Dai accepted the written pending plan and asked for the next weather check rather than pressing for a date which would make the council report easier. The surveyor gave her the checking interval and went down with his crew.

archive_19_023.speaker: narrator
archive_19_023.text: In the hall, the porter took off his cap and asked whether the archive had any account of a similar outlet collapse. Luo found a public maintenance description admitted for ordinary consultation. It named stone displacement after thaw, with its observations and later repair. The porter read slowly, touching the relevant line through the clean consultation strip rather than against the old paper. He wanted to know whether somebody had survived that older event. The text did not say. Luo resisted offering a comforting outcome it lacked and showed him where the recorded account ended.

archive_19_024.speaker: narrator
archive_19_024.text: The porter left with a permitted extract of the observations and a current district contact. Yue had expected his fear to turn into a lesson for everyone nearby. Instead he asked the cook whether the safe exit had better grit than the entrance. The cook pointed him towards the side path and made him wait while the duty worker checked its new frost. He left through the ordinary route with his cap pulled low. In the room behind him, the maintenance account returned to its wrapper and the next reader asked a completely different question about a garden wall.

archive_19_025.speaker: narrator
archive_19_025.text: That afternoon, Yue attended a scheduled clinical reassessment before seeking any heavier practice. The clinician examined the recovered calf's ordinary movement and asked what recent work it had actually done. Yue described light carrying, walking and the controlled fire-command task without claiming that a successful night had erased injury limits. The clinician cleared a gradual supervised practice assessment with rests and asked her to stop for pain or altered balance. It was permission to be assessed, not a verdict that every reinforced task had become safe.

archive_19_026.speaker: narrator
archive_19_026.text: Tan arranged the separate practice for the next morning in the dry assessed room, with the prepared training boards and inspected stop path. The interval belonged to Yue's agreed training time, not to a drainage assignment looking for free strength. Yue's fresh measure showed twenty-four available units before the rested assessment. She declined a longer series suggested by a curious assistant. She wanted to observe balance after the first rested set. The assistant looked disappointed until Tan asked whether she was attending a circus or helping someone return to a skill.

archive_19_027.speaker: narrator
archive_19_027.text: Yue began with unreinforced steps and measured release, moving slowly enough to feel the old inclination to favour one leg. Nothing hurt. Tan watched the soles rather than Yue's face, then asked her to rest and repeat the ordinary sequence. The next set used the inspected prepared stance within its existing quarter-unit useful-pulse rating and full-release limit. The checks used a quarter unit each; one half-unit gross command supplied the quarter-unit useful pulse, leaving twenty-three. No external load entered her channels. The boards stayed quiet, and the calf gave her information less dramatic than either fear or triumph.

archive_19_028.speaker: narrator
archive_19_028.text: After the rest interval, Tan checked the measure and asked Yue to turn only when the stop test showed full release. Yue did so, then sat instead of demonstrating a second unnecessary flourish. Her four-pair stage remained the one she had earned before the archive appointment. She had recovered a bounded use of an existing form, not discovered a new realm because a leg no longer hurt. Tan wrote the actual assessment result on the training card. Yue kept the card with her own practice notes rather than adding it to the archive's drainage proposal.

archive_19_029.speaker: lin_yue
archive_19_029.text: I thought recovery would feel like being handed back the person I was before the strain. It feels more like learning where that person hurried. The boards have not changed their rating because I waited beside a window for weeks. My impatience has not become a source of charge. I can make this short set cleanly and stop. That seems disappointingly small until I remember how much work a small mistake made the last time I wanted to finish quickly.

archive_19_030.speaker: narrator
archive_19_030.text: Tan said disappointment was cheaper than another injury and offered Yue the ordinary practice cloth. The assistant asked whether a mountain archive required every worker to cultivate. Dai, passing the door, said it required workers to know which tasks belonged to them. Several skilled staff had never formed a cultivated pair. The assistant looked towards the cook, who was carrying a heavy but ordinary pot with the proper handle and a second person's help. The cook told her to hold the door rather than watch competence as if it were a rare animal.

archive_19_031.speaker: narrator
archive_19_031.text: The new assessment changed Yue's private plans more than her assigned duties. She could begin modest practice intervals again within the agreed time. She could also refuse a task which exceeded the actual assessment without having to describe herself as permanently fragile. At supper, He Xi brought an outside delivery and left before the archive meal, going home to his parents' pot. He asked whether she was likely to return to road work after spring. Yue said she would know more when the term and roads were both real things rather than arguments about the future.

archive_19_032.speaker: narrator
archive_19_032.text: He Xi said his father had asked the same question about him. The question sounded as though he should choose either staying beside the rented room or remaining a courier forever. He wanted a route which let him earn reliably and come home some evenings. Yue asked whether such work existed. He said the lower relay might need a regular local loop when the seasonal freight reopened, but he had not applied. He was waiting to see whether his father's hand would improve, as though an improved hand would sign his own application for him.

archive_19_033.speaker: narrator
archive_19_033.text: She told him about asking for a date rather than a final promise. He listened, then said he would request the loop's actual terms before choosing. The ordinary messenger work still needed him tomorrow. He went down the cleared path with his parcel cover and no immediate revelation bright enough to impress a family. Yue returned to the residential table, where Luo had accidentally sewed one sleeve edge to the mending cloth. Dai examined the trap and said his robe had acquired an unauthorised deposit. He handed her the scissors.

archive_19_034.speaker: narrator
archive_19_034.text: The orchard representative came on the one hundred and thirtieth morning with the current occupant's condition report. The ordinary appointed survey had taken place in the house with his consent, recording the outer wall, roof and necessary repairs without copying his rooms into a public exhibit. One roof patch needed summer replacement, and the western lintel remained sound under its present use. The representative brought the actual surveyer's signed sheet and the occupant's chosen contact address. She asked whether the archive could provide the recovered condition clause beside it before the registry fixed the spring session.

archive_19_035.speaker: narrator
archive_19_035.text: Dai supplied the clause under the parties' established authority and asked the representative to read its maintenance requirement in full. The grandmother's descendant could continue occupation while keeping the stated school path usable and meeting the ordinary house upkeep. It did not require the descendant to own the surrounding orchard. It did not turn every public path expenditure into a charge payable to whichever person held the orchard books. The representative knew the words now. She wanted the hearing to examine which obligations the family had performed and which trustee expenses might be recoverable under the lawful arrangements.

archive_19_036.speaker: narrator
archive_19_036.text: He Xi's mother arrived for the agreed short source appointment, bringing her own household notebook. She had chosen the relevant dated path entries after the registry's request. Other family writing remained under her closed cover. Her son's father carried the light book bag within his recovered limit; he had offered the task without case payment. He Xi met them after his local loop. He wanted to look inside the notebook at once. His mother said she would open it at the table where the clerk could record what she actually chose.

archive_19_037.speaker: narrator
archive_19_037.text: The entries described drain clearing, replacement grit and a fence conversation from the years when the family still expected to return. Several were only reminders, with no receipts attached. The clerk distinguished paid work from a plan not confirmed as completed. The mother supplied two retained confirmations from the school's then caretaker and asked for their signatures to be checked through the comparison. She would not convert every scribbled intention into completed maintenance. He Xi looked disappointed at a crossed-out entry. His father said an abandoned plan was better left abandoned than made to carry weight it could not bear.

archive_19_038.speaker: narrator
archive_19_038.text: The mother had a memory of being told the descendant clause was no longer active. She remembered the trustee's receiving room and a chair with a broken rung. She did not remember the clerk's exact words or the exact date. Her dated enquiry copy established the season and request; the later registry search established what had happened to the instrument. The appointed writer asked whether she wanted her recollection included with those limits. She said yes, then heard the reading back and removed the adjective dismissive. She had felt dismissed. That did not preserve the person's tone exactly.

archive_19_039.speaker: narrator
archive_19_039.text: He Xi waited until the account was complete before asking whether the notebook meant the family had fulfilled the condition. The clerk said that was a question for the competent hearing, with the trustees able to answer the same evidence. His mother put the cover back on her notebook and said she preferred a question which somebody was finally required to decide. His father asked whether the return path had thawed by the narrow lane. The clerk checked the current watcher's note. Family disappointment and a dangerous patch of ice could occupy the same afternoon without either cancelling the other.

archive_19_040.speaker: narrator
archive_19_040.text: At the doorway, the orchard representative spoke to the mother without their sons' old arguments covering the conversation. She said the trustees had repaired an empty roof they believed their institution could lawfully let, and an old worker had paid rent believing the same thing. The mother said she had asked while it was still empty and had been refused an answer worth showing another office. They stood facing the yard's pale snow. Neither fact made the other vanish. The representative asked whether the hearing might include an arrangement giving the occupant time to move if the family right prevailed.

archive_19_041.speaker: narrator
archive_19_041.text: The mother said she would consider an actual proposal after hearing its terms. She would not promise to leave her family displaced forever because another person had been placed in the house later. She also did not want to arrive at her mother's door by sending an elderly worker into a winter lane. The representative nodded and said spring travel might allow an ordinary alternative through the orchard's own worker housing. That option needed a real vacancy and the occupant's answer. They agreed to ask for it before the hearing rather than present hope as a room already waiting.

archive_19_042.speaker: narrator
archive_19_042.text: He Xi heard only the last part and asked his mother whether she had given away their claim. She turned towards him sharply enough that his father took the book bag. She said considering a move date was not giving away the instrument; his father's slower rate had not given away his trade. He Xi looked at the bag and apologised without adding an excuse about how long they had waited. The representative left while the family spoke beside the steps. Yue stayed at the copying table. This conversation belonged to people who needed no added audience.

archive_19_043.speaker: narrator
archive_19_043.text: Dai wrote the requested institutional account in the late afternoon. It separated the source's earlier return into the wrong inner wrapper from her own catalogue abbreviation seven years ago. The family's initial fourteen-year-old enquiry predated that abbreviation. Her later entry had perpetuated an incomplete description and affected subsequent searches; it had not caused every earlier refusal. She wanted the account clear enough that the hearing could assign responsibility without finding a single convenient moment to blame. Luo checked the movement dates independently and returned one sentence which compressed three events into one.

archive_19_044.speaker: narrator
archive_19_044.text: He marked the three dates along the margin and asked Dai to put the actual people and actions back into the sentence. She did, though she disliked seeing a paragraph grow after spending decades teaching cataloguers to shorten theirs. The original return, inherited description and later abbreviated entry acquired separate lines. The correction then showed how each could be followed to its source. Yue made the clean copy after Dai signed it. The page sounded less elegant than the archive's old catalogue preface. It would be considerably easier to question at a table.

archive_19_045.speaker: narrator
archive_19_045.text: Sun's next appointment request concerned the spring hearing, with its audience and expected question listed. The registry wanted her bounded account of the public path agreement she had seen as a former copyist and the uncertainty she had retained about one ink-stained word. It did not ask her to pronounce on house possession. She could attend if the actual route and her ordinary walking guidance allowed, or choose a permitted written read-back instead. She asked for the proposed date before deciding, then returned to the umbrella story. Its owner had begun arguing with a patch.

archive_19_046.speaker: sun_nian
archive_19_046.text: They have asked whether I can recall a paper, which is sensible. If they ask whether I can recall everybody's intentions, I shall need a different pair of eyes and another seventy-four years. I may have been standing near a doorway when a person made a mistake. That does not mean the mistake left its full explanation in my head. Let the registry bring its dates. I can bring the part I chose to remember and say where it becomes uncertain.

archive_19_047.speaker: narrator
archive_19_047.text: The registry clerk acknowledged her requested limits and kept the spring appointment pending the common travel notice. Sun told Tan she might wear the plum robe because its pocket could hold her own reading glasses and the small umbrella notebook. Tan asked whether she wanted the story available at a legal hearing. Sun said no, but a person could become bored after her permitted evidence ended. She intended to remain a person during the waiting. Tan offered to mend the robe's pocket seam. Sun accepted the ordinary favour and supplied her own thread.

archive_19_048.speaker: narrator
archive_19_048.text: By the one hundred and thirty-first evening, the preparation bundle had a structure: instruments, verified movement chain, admitted upkeep records, current condition report and bounded witness offers. The parties retained their own copies and objections. There was no final ruling tucked into its cover. Luo labelled the bundle for the registrar's actual receiving office and prepared the safe local dispatch. Yue counted the permitted sheets beside the clerk, then watched him seal them. A winter's delayed question had acquired enough shape to travel towards an answer without requiring anyone at the archive to become the judge.

archive_19_049.speaker: narrator
archive_19_049.text: The workshop's repaired room passed its qualified inspection on the one hundred and thirty-second morning. The guard kept loose wrapping clear of the heating frame, the changed tool rest preserved the assessed reach and the receiver fitting passed its separate circuit check. The operator practised stopping the new feed before ordinary heating resumed. Tan attended under her permitted professional advice appointment, then left the workshop's responsible joiner and assessor to sign their own work. A sound diagram had supported the repair; it could not sign for the people who actually completed it.

archive_19_050.speaker: narrator
archive_19_050.text: The mutual-loss association settled the remaining fifteen copper against the accepted covered work and its receipts. Thirty had already been paid provisionally; forty-five was the total covered settlement, not forty-five more. The owner's remaining thirteen became twenty-eight before any later trading income. He kept that private cash record separate from the archive's advice receipt. Six old rear drawings remained lost, and the reconstructed hinge plate carried its current date and sources. The customer took his repaired cabinet home, after making the owner open the troublesome drawer once more in front of him.

archive_19_051.speaker: narrator
archive_19_051.text: He Xi's father received payment for his actual light bench intervals under the ordinary workshop rate and kept the recovery allowance line distinct. He had expected the fire to make an employer forget promises conveniently. The owner had expected the lost drawings to make every worker accuse him of something he could not answer. Their receipt was plain enough for both to examine. Neither called it friendship. The father asked for a steadier stool, and the owner found one which did not rock beside the altered bench. Work resumed around a small practical improvement.

archive_19_052.speaker: narrator
archive_19_052.text: At the archive, the lower treasurer arrived during the authorised settlement sitting with Yue's winter appointment and the checked roster. It covered ninety-six days, from the thirty-seventh through the one hundred and thirty-second inclusive, at five copper a day. Rest days and the accepted recovery interval had remained paid under its actual terms. The treasurer counted four hundred and eighty copper and let Yue count it again before signing. She had earned it by fulfilling the appointment, with its protections, rather than by never becoming tired or hurt.

archive_19_053.speaker: narrator
archive_19_053.text: Yue kept the separate receipt beside the earlier first-term payment of one hundred and eighty. The reserved return fare remained her own eight copper, not a deduction taken again from the new wages. Her accepted spring extension would begin the next day and cover fifty-six further days for two hundred and eighty, payable under that separate funded agreement. Tomorrow happened to be her weekly rest. Signing an earlier extension had not moved that cycle, and payment today had not purchased tomorrow's free hours. She asked the treasurer to verify the dates aloud to hear how ordinary they sounded.

archive_19_054.speaker: lin_yue
archive_19_054.text: When I arrived, thirty-six days sounded like something I could fit into a traveller's life without changing it. Ninety-six sounded much longer, so I made myself look at every provision before I stayed. Now fifty-six more lies on the table, already chosen, with its own paid work and rest. I have not become somebody who belongs to a mountain because a mountain kept her busy. I have been employed here, lived here and wanted things here. That is enough to make leaving or staying a real choice.

archive_19_055.speaker: narrator
archive_19_055.text: The treasurer signed the winter wage line complete and retained the unused qualified-work and contingency balances in their original authorised account. One hundred and two for qualified work and one hundred and thirty-eight contingency remained subject to that authority's further decision; they did not drift into the separate spring goods, wages or work fund. Dai supplied the actual winter receipts and the closed roof-work statement. The treasurer asked two questions about dates and obtained both references before packing the book. The sound of counted coins gave way to the ordinary scrape of chairs.

archive_19_056.speaker: narrator
archive_19_056.text: Yue placed most of her earned money in her own securely tied purse and kept the next modest spending amount separate. She had planned to celebrate by buying something useful, then became annoyed at the idea that every earned coin had to justify itself through usefulness. She might buy fresh fruit when the route reopened. She might replace the mouse-coloured stockings if they proved uncomfortable. She might send home a small parcel chosen for her mother. For that afternoon, she put the purse away and went downstairs to find the meal.

archive_19_057.speaker: narrator
archive_19_057.text: The cook had prepared beans with a little dried plum, changing their familiar flavour without creating an uncounted feast. Ten resident shares came out of the actual store. The cook said Yue could admire her purse after collecting a bowl. Sun was visiting for tea only and brought her own bought biscuit, which she refused to call a ceremonial wage cake. Luo asked whether one bite could be licensed. She said he could negotiate with the biscuit if it had agreed to remain intact. Tan watched him consider the joke and rescued the plate.

archive_19_058.speaker: narrator
archive_19_058.text: After the meal, the residents helped put the winter report in order before returning to their own tasks. The roof repair had remained dry through the later corridor incident; the separate retaining outlet still awaited its qualified thaw work. Public references stayed open under the agreed schedule. Private deposits followed their owners' distinct directions. Two regional cases remained on their mutually renewed loan, and six public originals awaited safe carriage. Dai asked that the report end with the next actual checks rather than an adjective announcing victory over weather. Outside, the afternoon frost began tightening the gutter again.

archive_19_059.speaker: narrator
archive_19_059.text: The storekeeper's closing count recorded six hundred and sixty-nine and a half food shares, fifty-four and a half usable charcoal sacks and eighty-one and a half cooking bundles. Seven days had taken seventy resident shares and seven bundles; three milder days had used one and a half charcoal sacks, then four colder days had used four. No archive meal guests had been added. All spring supplies were accepted and paid. Yue checked the signed issue sheet against the count, then left the book on the shelf where the cook could reach it without asking permission to feed people.

archive_19_060.speaker: narrator
archive_19_060.text: In her room that evening, she tried the new stockings. Their colour remained dismal, but the seams sat smoothly beneath her boot. She put the boots away instead of beginning an unnecessary practice set. The next day belonged to her weekly rest at the start of a term she had already accepted. From downstairs came Luo's complaint that the mending scissors had developed a preference for his fingers. Dai told him to let the cloth lie flat. Yue opened her mother's letter, smiled at the chicken argument and began choosing what she wanted to write back next.
